title: Product Engineering Durable Jobs and Revenue Safety Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A provider finished an export; the worker crashed before recording success. What is the safest retry plan?

options.label: Reconcile via a stable provider key or operation ID before repeating the effect.
Always generate again because the queue redelivered.
Mark success without checking whether an output exists.

questions.explanation: Redelivery proves the message needs handling, not that the external effect failed. Reconcile a stable operation identity where supported. Otherwise keep the uncertainty explicit; neither blind retries nor invented success preserve correctness.

questions.prompt: The API writes a job, then crashes before publishing its queue message. Which design closes this gap?

options.label: Publish first and assume the database write will succeed.
Keep the queue message only in the browser tab.
Commit the job, credit reservation, and outbox record atomically.

questions.explanation: An atomic job/reservation/outbox transaction leaves durable dispatch intent after a crash. Publishing first can create work without an accepted job or reservation. A tab cannot preserve the backend acceptance contract.

questions.prompt: Two workspaces reuse the same idempotency key. What is the correct boundary?

options.label: Scope the key to the workspace and compare the request fingerprint.
Use one global key namespace and return the first workspace’s result.

questions.explanation: Tenant scope prevents unrelated requests colliding or leaking results. A body fingerprint detects changed requests under the same key. Prompt text omits workspace, input revision, model, and configuration identity.

questions.prompt: Worker A pauses, its lease expires, and worker B commits success. A resumes. What protects the result?

options.label: A guarded state transition with the current attempt/fencing token.
A lease timestamp alone, with no check at commit.
Whichever worker writes last should win.

questions.explanation: A lease can expire while its previous holder is still running. The commit must validate attempt ownership and state/version, so stale workers cannot overwrite B. Last-write-wins is unsafe for results and ledger transitions.

questions.prompt: A webhook names a real job but its authenticity is unverified. What should happen before charging?

options.label: Trust the job ID as a secret signature.
Charge immediately, then log the sender address.
Verify supported authentication or reconcile through an authenticated status read.

questions.explanation: A job ID identifies a resource; it does not authenticate the sender or prove completion. Verify the documented delivery authentication or fetch authoritative status. Logging after charging cannot prevent a forged side effect.

questions.prompt: After a deploy, p95 preview latency rises while inference duration is flat. What should you inspect first?

options.label: Ignore the problem because every HTTP request returns 200.
Per-stage traces and cohort changes across queueing, transfer, decode, and render.
Buy GPUs before measuring any other stage.

questions.explanation: End-to-end latency includes stages outside inference. Compare deployment cohorts and traces to locate the increase. More GPU capacity may not help, and successful HTTP delivery does not prove a timely usable preview.
